mock_data.title: The Right to Die
mock_data.passage:
Recent legislation by the European Union on human rights has led more and more people to invoke these rights. In Britain, the most recently invoked of these is the right to die.

Currently, a woman is trying to prove that the British government is breaching the European Convention on Human Rights by causing her to go on living in inhuman and degrading circumstances. She is suffering from motor neurone disease, an incurable and fatal wasting disease.

The woman is claiming the right to die with dignity at the time of her choice. Having lost the use of most of her bodily functions, although her mind is still functioning, she wishes to be allowed to take her own life, since she no longer enjoys any quality of life. However, her physical condition is such that she cannot commit suicide without some help. Her wish is that the courts will agree in advance not to prosecute her husband if he helps her die.

She is being backed in her court appeal by the Voluntary Euthanasia Society. Its members feel that euthanasia should be a real possibility for people who are in the final stages of terminal illnesses, and who are in such severe pain or in a state of such total incapacity that they do not wish to go on living. They should legally be allowed to resort to assisted suicide, possibly physician-assisted suicide.

Over the years, many arguments have been put forward for legalizing euthanasia, but people are afraid that this might give rise to murder, unless there were very strict safeguards. Mercy killing is illegal in most countries although it was recently made legal in the Netherlands.

Several countries are currently considering the issue of living wills. Such documents are prepared by people when they are quite well and indicate that they wish to invoke the right to die, or the right to be helped to die, if they ever reach a stage at which death would come as a welcome release from some terrible incurable condition. The decision of the courts in this case is not yet known. One thing is certain. The debate on this sad subject will continue.
mock_data.passageB1:
Laws about human rights in Europe are making more people talk about these rights. In Britain, one of the newest rights people are talking about is the right to die.

Now, a woman is trying to show that the British government is not respecting her human rights. She says they are making her live in a way that is inhuman and makes her feel bad. She has a disease called motor neurone disease. This disease cannot be cured and will cause her body to waste away.

The woman wants the right to die with dignity when she chooses. She can't use most of her body anymore, but her mind is still clear. She wants to be allowed to end her life because she doesn't enjoy life anymore. But she is too weak to do it alone. She wants the court to promise that her husband won't be punished if he helps her to die.

A group called the Voluntary Euthanasia Society is helping her with her court appeal. They think that euthanasia should be an option for people who are very sick and near the end of their lives. If they are in a lot of pain or can't do anything for themselves, and they don't want to live, they should be allowed to have help to die. This could be assisted suicide, where a doctor helps them.

Over the years, people have given many reasons for making euthanasia legal. But some people are afraid that it could lead to murder if there aren't strong rules. Mercy killing is against the law in most countries, but it is legal in the Netherlands.

Some countries are thinking about living wills. These are documents that people write when they are healthy. In them, they say that if they ever get a very bad, incurable disease, they want the right to die or to get help to die. They want death to be a release from their suffering. We don't know what the court will decide in this case yet. But one thing is sure: people will keep talking about this difficult subject.
mock_data.passageB2:
Recent changes in European Union human rights laws have led to more people asserting their rights. In Britain, the most recent example of this is the invocation of the right to die.

Currently, a woman is trying to prove that the British government is violating the European Convention on Human Rights by forcing her to live in what she considers inhumane and degrading conditions. She suffers from motor neurone disease, a disease that inevitably leads to death and the gradual loss of muscle function.

The woman is demanding the right to die with dignity, at a time of her choosing. Having lost the ability to control most of her body, although her mind is still clear, she wants to be allowed to end her own life, arguing that her quality of life is now unacceptable. However, her physical condition prevents her from committing suicide without assistance. She hopes the courts will agree not to prosecute her husband if he helps her to die. This is also called assisted dying.

Her court case is supported by the Voluntary Euthanasia Society. Its members believe that euthanasia should be a genuine option for people in the final stages of terminal illnesses, who are experiencing such severe pain or such a complete loss of ability that they no longer wish to live. They argue that such people should be legally allowed access to assisted suicide, possibly with the help of a doctor.

Over the years, many arguments have been made in favour of legalising euthanasia, but some people fear that it could pave the way for murder, unless strict safeguards were in place. Mercy killing, also known as euthanasia, is illegal in most countries, although it has recently been legalised in the Netherlands.

Several countries are currently considering the issue of advance directives, sometimes called 'living wills'. These documents are created by people while they are healthy, stating that they wish to exercise their right to die, or to be helped to die, if they ever reach a point where death would be a welcome relief from a terrible and incurable condition. The court's decision in this case is still pending. One thing is certain: the debate on this difficult and emotional subject will continue to rage.
mock_data.passageC1:
The escalating influence of European Union human rights legislation has, in recent years, seen a corresponding increase in the invocation of these rights by individuals across member states. In Britain, the most recent and arguably most contentious application of these principles concerns the so-called right to die, a concept fraught with ethical and legal complexities.

Currently, a woman afflicted with motor neurone disease, a debilitating and invariably fatal condition, is challenging the British government's stance. Her argument hinges on the assertion that the state, by compelling her continued existence under what she considers inhuman and degrading circumstances, is in contravention of the European Convention on Human Rights. The crux of her appeal lies in the desire to exercise autonomy over her own demise.

The claimant seeks the right to terminate her life with dignity, at a time of her choosing. Despite retaining full cognitive function, the progressive loss of bodily control has, in her view, rendered her life devoid of quality. Crucially, her physical limitations preclude her from independently ending her life, thereby necessitating assistance. Her plea to the courts is for a guarantee of non-prosecution for her husband, should he provide such aid. This raises profound ethical questions regarding the boundaries of personal autonomy and the role of the state in protecting vulnerable individuals.

Lending their support to this legal challenge is the Voluntary Euthanasia Society, an organization advocating for the legalization of euthanasia for individuals in the terminal stages of illness. Members contend that those enduring intractable pain or profound incapacity should have the legal option of assisted suicide, potentially including physician-assisted suicide. However, the prospect of opening Pandora's Box with such legislation remains a significant concern for many.

Over the years, the debate surrounding the legalization of euthanasia has been punctuated by numerous arguments, both for and against. A primary concern is the potential for abuse, with critics suggesting that legalization could pave the way for non-voluntary euthanasia, effectively amounting to murder. To mitigate this risk, proponents typically advocate for stringent safeguards, although the precise nature and effectiveness of such measures remain a subject of considerable debate. While mercy killing remains illegal in most countries, the Netherlands recently broke new ground by legalizing it, a move that has been met with both praise and condemnation.

The concept of living wills, also known as advance directives, is gaining traction in several countries. These documents, drafted by individuals while of sound mind, articulate their wishes regarding end-of-life care, specifically their desire to invoke the right to die or to receive assistance in doing so, should they reach a point where death offers a welcome reprieve from an unbearable, incurable condition. As the courts deliberate on this particular case, one thing remains unequivocally clear: the complex and emotionally charged debate surrounding the right to die is set to persist indefinitely, forcing society to grapple with fundamental questions about life, death, and individual liberty. The case underscores the need for a nuanced and compassionate approach to end-of-life care.

mock_data.translation:
Yevropa Ittifoqi tomonidan inson huquqlari bo'yicha qabul qilingan so'nggi qonunchilik tobora ko'proq odamlarni bu huquqlardan foydalanishga undamoqda. Buyuk Britaniyada eng so'nggi qo'llanilgan huquq o'lish huquqidir.

Hozirda bir ayol Britaniya hukumati uni g'ayriinsoniy va kamsituvchi sharoitlarda yashashga majbur qilish orqali Yevropa Inson Huquqlari Konventsiyasini buzayotganini isbotlashga harakat qilmoqda. U motor neyron kasalligidan aziyat chekmoqda, bu davolanmaydigan va halokatli zaif kasallikdir.

Ayol o'zi tanlagan vaqtda qadr-qimmat bilan o'lish huquqini talab qilmoqda. Aqliy qobiliyatlari hali ham ishlayotgan bo'lsa-da, tana funktsiyalarining ko'p qismini yo'qotgan holda, u endi hayot sifatidan bahramand bo'lmaganligi sababli o'z joniga qasd qilishiga ruxsat berilishini xohlaydi. Biroq, uning jismoniy holati shundayki, u yordam olmasdan o'z joniga qasd qila olmaydi. Uning istagi shuki, sudlar agar eri unga o'lishda yordam bersa, uni oldidan jinoiy ta'qib qilmaslikka oldindan rozi bo'lsin.

U o'z sud apellyatsiyasida Ixtiyoriy Evtanaziya Jamiyati tomonidan qo'llab-quvvatlanmoqda. Uning a'zolari evtanaziya terminal kasaliklarning oxirgi bosqichida bo'lgan va shunday og'ir og'riq yoki to'liq qobiliyatsizlik holatida bo'lgan odamlar uchun haqiqiy imkoniyat bo'lishi kerakligini his qilishadi, ular yashashni xohlamaydilar. Ularga qonuniy ravishda yordamli o'z joniga qasd qilish, ehtimol shifokor yordamidagi o'z joniga qasd qilish imkoniyati berilishi kerak.

Yillar davomida evtanaziyani qonuniylashtirish uchun ko'plab dalillar ilgari surildi, ammo odamlar bu juda qattiq himoya choralari bo'lmasa, qotillikka olib kelishi mumkinligidan qo'rqishadi. Rahm-shafqat bilan o'ldirish ko'pgina mamlakatlarda noqonuniydir, garchi u yaqinda Niderlandiyada qonuniy qilindi.

Bir nechta mamlakatlar hozirda hayotiy vasiyatlar masalasini ko'rib chiqmoqdalar. Bunday hujjatlar odamlar sog'lom bo'lganlarida tayyorlanadi va ular agar davolanmaydigan dahshatli holatdan qutulib qolish uchun o'lim xush kelibdi deb hisoblangan bosqichga yetsalar, o'lish huquqidan foydalanishni yoki o'lishda yordam berilishini istashlarini ko'rsatadi. Ushbu ishdagi sudlarning qarori hali noma'lum. Bir narsa aniq. Ushbu qayg'uli mavzu bo'yicha munozaralar davom etadi.

rules.definition: Instructions that say what you are allowed to do and what you are not allowed to do.

punished.example: He was punished for his crimes.
punished.definition: To make someone suffer because they have done something wrong.

difficult.definition: Not easy to do or understand.

euthanasia.definition: The act of killing someone painlessly, especially someone who is very ill and wants to die.

waste away.example: The illness caused her to waste away.

waste away.exampleUzbek: Kasallik uning ozib ketishiga sabab bo'ldi.

end her life.example: She decided to end her life because she was in so much pain.
end her life.exampleUzbek: U juda ko'p og'riq azobida bo'lgani uchun hayotiga nuqta qo'yishga qaror qildi.

human rights.example: Everyone should have their human rights respected.
human rights.definition: Basic rights that everyone should have, such as the right to freedom and to be treated fairly.
human rights.exampleUzbek: Har bir insonning inson huquqlari hurmat qilinishi kerak.

living wills.example: She prepared a living will to state her wishes.
living wills.definition: A legal document that says what medical treatment you would want if you were unable to make decisions for yourself.
living wills.exampleUzbek: U o'z xohishlarini bildirish uchun tiriklar vasiyatnomasini tayyorladi.

right to die.example: The right to die is a controversial topic.
right to die.definition: The idea that a person should be allowed to choose to end their own life, especially if they have a terminal illness.

mercy killing.example: Mercy killing is illegal in most countries.
mercy killing.definition: Killing someone who is very ill in order to stop them from suffering.
mercy killing.exampleUzbek: Rahmdillik bilan o'ldirish ko'pgina davlatlarda noqonuniy.

assisted suicide.uzbek: Yordam bilan o'z joniga qasd qilish
assisted suicide.example: Assisted suicide is illegal in many countries.
assisted suicide.exampleUzbek: Ko'pgina davlatlarda yordam bilan o'z joniga qasd qilish noqonuniy.

rage.example: The debate about euthanasia will continue to rage.

relief.uzbek: Xavotir yoki qayg'udan ozod bo'lgandan keyin paydo bo'ladigan ishonch va xotirjamlik hissi.
relief.example: The news brought a great sense of relief.
relief.definition: A feeling of reassurance and relaxation following release from anxiety or distress.
relief.exampleUzbek: Bu xabar katta yengillik hissini keltirdi.

pending.example: The court's decision is still pending.

exercise.uzbek: (Huquq, kuch yoki sifatni) ishlatish yoki qo'llash.
exercise.example: Patients should exercise their right to choose their treatment.
exercise.definition: Use or apply (a right, power, or quality).
exercise.exampleUzbek: Bemorlar davolanishni tanlash huquqidan foydalanishlari kerak.

inhumane.uzbek: Shafqatsiz va vahshiy; azob-uqubatlarga rahm-shafqat ko'rsatmaslik.
inhumane.example: The prisoners were kept in inhumane conditions.
inhumane.definition: Cruel and brutal; without compassion for suffering.

access to.uzbek: Biror narsadan foydalanish yoki biror joyga kirish imkoniyati yoki huquqi.
access to.example: Everyone should have access to clean water.
access to.definition: The opportunity or right to use something or enter a place.
access to.exampleUzbek: Har kim toza suvdan foydalanish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lishi kerak.

asserting.uzbek: Qat'iy va kuch bilan huquq yoki faktni ta'kidlash
asserting.example: She was asserting her independence from her parents.
asserting.definition: Stating a right or fact confidently and forcefully

degrading.example: It's degrading to have to ask for money.
degrading.definition: Causing someone to feel ashamed and humiliated.

demanding.uzbek: Biror narsani kuch bilan so'rash, go'yo u o'ziga tegishlidek.
demanding.example: The workers are demanding better pay.
demanding.definition: Requesting something forcefully, as if it were one's due.

inevitably.uzbek: Sodir bo'lishi aniq bo'lganidek; muqarrar ravishda.
inevitably.example: Stress inevitably leads to health problems.
inevitably.definition: As is certain to happen; unavoidably.
inevitably.exampleUzbek: Stress muqarrar ravishda sog'liq muammolariga olib keladi.

invocation.uzbek: O'z ishingizni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun biror narsaga, ayniqsa qonun yoki printsipga murojaat qilish harakati.
invocation.example: The invocation of human rights is becoming more common.
invocation.definition: The act of referring to something, especially a law or principle, in order to support your case.
invocation.exampleUzbek: Inson huquqlariga murojaat qilish tobora keng tarqalmoqda.

safeguards.uzbek: Kimnidir yoki biror narsani himoya qilish yoki istalmagan narsaning oldini olish uchun ko'rilgan choralar.
safeguards.example: We need to put safeguards in place to prevent fraud.
safeguards.definition: Measures taken to protect someone or something or to prevent something undesirable.
safeguards.exampleUzbek: Biz firibgarlikning oldini olish uchun himoya choralari ko'rishimiz kerak.

gradual loss.uzbek: Sekin va progressiv pasayish yoki yo'qolish.
gradual loss.example: The patient experienced a gradual loss of memory.
gradual loss.definition: A slow and progressive decline or disappearance.

unacceptable.exampleUzbek: Uning xulq-atvori butunlay qabul qilinishi mumkin emas edi.

mercy killing.uzbek: Azobni engillashtirish uchun odamning hayotiga qasddan chek qo'yish harakati.
mercy killing.example: Mercy killing is illegal in many countries.
mercy killing.definition: The act of deliberately ending a person's life to relieve suffering.
mercy killing.exampleUzbek: Rahmdillik o'ldirishi ko'plab mamlakatlarda noqonuniy hisoblanadi.

assisted dying.uzbek: O'z hayotiga chek qo'ymoqchi bo'lgan odamga yordam ko'rsatish.
assisted dying.example: Assisted dying is a controversial issue.
assisted dying.definition: Providing assistance to someone who wishes to end their life.

genuine option.example: Euthanasia should be a genuine option for terminally ill patients.
genuine option.exampleUzbek: Evtanazi terminal kasalliklar bilan og'rigan bemorlar uchun haqiqiy tanlov bo'lishi kerak.

pave the way for.uzbek: Biror narsaning sodir bo'lishi uchun shart-sharoitlar yoki imkoniyatlar yaratish.
pave the way for.example: These reforms will pave the way for economic growth.
pave the way for.definition: Create the conditions or opportunities for something to happen.
pave the way for.exampleUzbek: Ushbu islohotlar iqtisodiy o'sishga yo'l ochadi.

advance directives.uzbek: Odatda tiriklayin vasiyatnomani o'z ichiga olgan tibbiy muolajalar bo'yicha shaxsning istaklari to'g'risidagi yozma bayonot, agar shaxs ularni shifokorga etkazish imkoniga ega bo'lmasa, ushbu istaklar bajarilishini ta'minlash uchun tuziladi.
advance directives.example: It is important to prepare advance directives while you are still healthy.
advance directives.definition: A written statement of a person's wishes regarding medical treatment, often including a living will, made to ensure those wishes are carried out should the person be unable to communicate them to a doctor.
advance directives.exampleUzbek: Sog'lom bo'lganingizda oldindan ko'rsatmalarni tayyorlash muhimdir.

reprieve.uzbek: Zarardan yoki noqulaylikdan vaqtinchalik xalos bo'lish.
reprieve.example: The rain provided a brief reprieve from the scorching heat.
reprieve.definition: A temporary relief from harm or discomfort.
reprieve.exampleUzbek: Yomg'ir jazirama issiqdan qisqa muddatli xalos bo'lishni ta'minladi.

debilitating.uzbek: Kimdirni zaif va xasta qilib qo'yadigan.
debilitating.example: The disease had a debilitating effect on her physical strength.
debilitating.definition: Causing someone to become weak and infirm.
debilitating.exampleUzbek: Kasallik uning jismoniy kuchiga zaiflashtiruvchi ta'sir ko'rsatdi.

right to die.example: The debate over the right to die involves complex ethical and legal considerations.
right to die.definition: The asserted right of a person to choose to end their own life, typically in cases of terminal illness or unbearable suffering.
right to die.exampleUzbek: O'z joniga qasd qilish huquqi to'g'risidagi bahslar murakkab axloqiy va huquqiy mulohazalarni o'z ichiga oladi.

broke new ground.example: Her research broke new ground in the field of genetics.

intractable pain.example: The patient suffered from intractable pain despite receiving strong medication.

intractable pain.exampleUzbek: Bemorda kuchli dorilar qabul qilganiga qaramay, chidab bo'lmas og'riq bor edi.

pave the way for.definition: To create the conditions or opportunities for something to happen.

mock_data.translationB1:
Yevropada inson huquqlari haqidagi qonunlar odamlarni bu huquqlar haqida ko'proq gapirishga undamoqda. Britaniyada odamlar gapirayotgan eng yangi huquqlardan biri bu o'lish huquqi.

Hozirda bir ayol Britaniya hukumati uning inson huquqlarini hurmat qilmayotganini ko'rsatishga harakat qilmoqda. Uning aytishicha, ular uni insonparvarlikka zid bo'lgan tarzda yashashga majbur qilishmoqda va bu unga yomon ta'sir qilmoqda. Uning motor neyron kasalligi bor. Bu kasallikni davolab bo'lmaydi va uning tanasi so'lib borishiga sabab bo'ladi.

Ayol o'zi tanlagan vaqtda qadr-qimmat bilan o'lish huquqiga ega bo'lishni xohlaydi. U endi tanasining ko'p qismini ishlata olmaydi, lekin ongi hali ham tiniq. U hayotdan zavqlanmagani uchun hayotini tugatishga ruxsat berilishini xohlaydi. Ammo u buni yolg'iz o'zi qila olmaydi. U sud uning eriga, agar u unga o'lishga yordam bersa, jazolanmasligiga va'da berishini xohlaydi.

Ko'ngilli Evtanaziya Jamiyati deb nomlangan guruh unga sud shikoyati bilan yordam bermoqda. Ularning fikricha, evtanaziya juda kasal va hayotining oxiriga yaqin bo'lgan odamlar uchun variant bo'lishi kerak. Agar ular juda ko'p og'riq his qilsalar yoki o'zlari uchun hech narsa qila olmasalar va yashashni xohlamasalar, ularga o'lishga yordam berishga ruxsat berilishi kerak. Bu shifokor ularga yordam beradigan yordamli o'z joniga qasd qilish bo'lishi mumkin.

Yillar davomida odamlar evtanaziyani qonuniylashtirish uchun ko'plab sabablar keltirishgan. Ammo ba'zi odamlar, agar kuchli qoidalar bo'lmasa, bu qotillikka olib kelishi mumkinligidan qo'rqishadi. Ko'pgina mamlakatlarda rahmdillik bilan o'ldirish qonunga zid, ammo Gollandiyada qonuniy.

Ba'zi mamlakatlar hayotiy vasiyatnomalar haqida o'ylashmoqda. Bular odamlar sog'lom bo'lganida yozadigan hujjatlardir. Ularda, agar ularga juda yomon, davolab bo'lmaydigan kasallik yuqsa, o'lish yoki o'lishga yordam olish huquqiga ega bo'lishni xohlashlarini aytishadi. Ular o'limni azoblaridan xalos bo'lish deb bilishadi. Biz sud bu ishda nima qaror chiqarishini hali bilmaymiz. Ammo bir narsa aniq: odamlar bu qiyin mavzu haqida gapirishda davom etishadi.
mock_data.translationB2:
Yevropa Ittifoqining inson huquqlari to'g'risidagi qonunlariga kiritilgan so'nggi o'zgartirishlar ko'proq odamlarning o'z huquqlarini talab qilishiga olib keldi. Britaniyada buning eng so'nggi namunasi - o'lish huquqini qo'llash.

Ayni paytda bir ayol Britaniya hukumatini Yevropa Inson Huquqlari Konvensiyasini buzganlikda ayblashga harakat qilmoqda, chunki hukumat uni o'zi insoniyatga zid va kamsituvchi deb hisoblagan sharoitlarda yashashga majbur qilmoqda. U motor neyron kasalligidan aziyat chekmoqda, bu kasallik muqarrar ravishda o'limga va mushak funksiyalarining asta-sekin yo'qolishiga olib keladi.

Ayol o'z xohishiga ko'ra, munosib tarzda o'lish huquqini talab qilmoqda. Aqli hali tiniq bo'lsa-da, tanasining ko'p qismini boshqarish qobiliyatini yo'qotgan holda, u o'z hayotiga chek qo'yishga ruxsat berilishini istaydi va hayot sifatini hozirda qabul qilib bo'lmas deb ta'kidlamoqda. Biroq, uning jismoniy holati yordamisiz o'z joniga qasd qilishga yo'l qo'ymaydi. U sudlar, agar eri unga o'lishga yordam bersa, uni jazolamaslikka rozi bo'lishiga umid qilmoqda. Bu, shuningdek, yordam bilan o'lish deb ham ataladi.

Uning sud ishini Ko'ngilli Evtanaziya Jamiyati qo'llab-quvvatlaydi. Uning a'zolari evtanaziya o'limga olib keluvchi kasalliklarning so'nggi bosqichlarida bo'lgan, shunday kuchli og'riqni yoki qobiliyatini shunchalik to'liq yo'qotgan odamlar uchun haqiqiy imkoniyat bo'lishi kerak deb hisoblashadi, ular endi yashashni istamaydilar. Ularning ta'kidlashicha, bunday odamlarga yordam berilgan o'z joniga qasd qilishga qonuniy ravishda ruxsat berilishi kerak, ehtimol shifokor yordamida.

Yillar davomida evtanaziyani qonuniylashtirish foydasiga ko'plab dalillar keltirildi, ammo ba'zi odamlar, agar qat'iy himoya choralari ko'rilmasa, bu qotillikka yo'l ochishi mumkinligidan xavotirda. Rahmdillik bilan o'ldirish, ya'ni evtanaziya ko'pgina mamlakatlarda noqonuniy hisoblanadi, garchi yaqinda Gollandiyada qonuniylashtirilgan bo'lsa ham.

Hozirda bir nechta mamlakatlar oldindan ko'rsatmalar, ba'zan "tirik vasiyatnomalar" masalasini ko'rib chiqmoqda. Bu hujjatlar odamlar sog'lom bo'lganida yaratiladi va agar ular o'lim dahshatli va davolab bo'lmaydigan holatdan xalos etuvchi bo'ladigan nuqtaga etib borsalar, o'zlarining o'lish huquqlarini amalga oshirishni yoki o'lishga yordam berilishini xohlashlarini bildiradi. Ushbu ish bo'yicha sud qarori hali kutilmoqda. Bir narsa aniq: bu qiyin va hissiy mavzu bo'yicha bahs avjiga chiqishda davom etadi.
mock_data.translationC1:
Yevropa Ittifoqi inson huquqlari qonunchiligining ta'siri kuchayishi so'nggi yillarda a'zo davlatlardagi shaxslar tomonidan bu huquqlarning qo'llanilishi ortishiga olib keldi. Britaniyada bu tamoyillarning eng so'nggi va bahsli qo'llanilishi "o'lish huquqi" deb ataladigan tushunchaga tegishli bo'lib, u axloqiy va huquqiy murakkabliklarga to'la.

Hozirda motor neyron kasalligiga chalingan ayol, zaiflashtiruvchi va doimiy ravishda o'limga olib keladigan kasallik bilan Britaniya hukumatining pozitsiyasiga qarshi chiqmoqda. Uning argumenti shundan iboratki, davlat uni insoniylikka zid va kamsituvchi sharoitlarda yashashga majburlash orqali Inson huquqlari bo'yicha Yevropa konventsiyasini buzmoqda. Uning murojaatining mohiyati o'z o'limi ustidan avtonomiyani amalga oshirish istagida.

Da'vogar o'z hayotini o'zi tanlagan vaqtda munosib tarzda tugatish huquqini talab qilmoqda. To'liq kognitiv funktsiyani saqlab qolganiga qaramay, tanani nazorat qilishning progressiv yo'qolishi, uning fikricha, uning hayotini sifatdan mahrum qilgan. Muhimi shundaki, uning jismoniy cheklovlari unga mustaqil ravishda hayotini tugatishga to'sqinlik qiladi, shuning uchun yordam zarur. Uning sudlarga murojaati - agar u shunday yordam ko'rsatsa, eri uchun jinoiy javobgarlikka tortilmaslik kafolati. Bu shaxsiy avtonomiya chegaralari va zaif shaxslarni himoya qilishda davlatning roli haqida chuqur axloqiy savollarni tug'diradi.

Evtanaziyani qonuniylashtirish tarafdori bo'lgan tashkilot - "Ko'ngilli evtanaziya jamiyati" ushbu huquqiy muammoga o'z yordamini bermoqda. A'zolar davolab bo'lmaydigan og'riq yoki chuqur nogironlikka duchor bo'lganlar o'z joniga qasd qilishning qonuniy variantiga ega bo'lishi kerak, bu potentsial ravishda shifokor yordamida o'z joniga qasd qilishni ham o'z ichiga olishi mumkin. Biroq, bunday qonunchilik bilan Pandora qutisining ochilishi ko'pchilik uchun jiddiy tashvish bo'lib qolmoqda.

Yillar davomida evtanaziyani qonuniylashtirish bo'yicha munozaralar ko'plab argumentlar bilan ajralib turdi, ham tarafdor, ham qarshi. Asosiy tashvish suiiste'mol qilish potentsiali bo'lib, tanqidchilarning ta'kidlashicha, qonuniylashtirish yo'l ochishi mumkin majburiy bo'lmagan evtanaziya uchun, aslida qotillikka teng. Ushbu xavfni kamaytirish uchun tarafdorlar odatda qat'iy himoya choralarini qo'llashni yoqlashadi, garchi bunday chora-tadbirlarning aniq tabiati va samaradorligi muhim munozara mavzusi bo'lib qolmoqda. Ko'pgina mamlakatlarda rahm-shafqat o'ldirish noqonuniy bo'lib qolayotgan bo'lsa-da, yaqinda Niderlandiya uni qonuniylashtirish orqali yangi zamin yaratdi, bu qadam ham maqtovga, ham qoralashga sabab bo'ldi.

Tirik vasiyatlar, shuningdek, oldindan ko'rsatmalar deb ham ataladi, bir nechta mamlakatlarda ommalashib bormoqda. Ushbu hujjatlar aqli raso bo'lgan shaxslar tomonidan tuziladi, hayotning oxiridagi g'amxo'rlik bo'yicha o'z istaklarini, xususan, o'lish huquqini talab qilish yoki bunga yordam olish istagini, agar ular o'lim qabul qilinadigan darajaga etsa, qutulish chidab bo'lmas, davosi yo'q holatdan. Sudlar bu ishni muhokama qilayotgan ekan, bir narsa shubhasiz aniq: o'lish huquqi atrofidagi murakkab va hissiy munozaralar cheksiz davom etishi kutilmoqda va jamiyatni hayot, o'lim va shaxsiy erkinlik haqidagi asosiy savollar bilan kurashishga majbur qiladi. Ish hayot oxiridagi g'amxo'rlikka nisbatan nozik va rahmdil yondashuv zarurligini ta'kidlaydi.
